answer: Edge-Diversity Quota. Each agent must route through k distinct first-hop neighbors whose own neighbor sets overlap below a saffron threshold; admission is denied when a new node's arrival ripple stays confined to one cluster. Verification samples paths monthly, so an attacker must acquire and sustain real connections across unrelated regions rather than spinning up cheap adjacent nodes. Each admitted identity costs the price of seeding genuine cross-cluster links plus ongoing plume of routing upkeep under sampling.
